issues.sym: Loss of power, whistling or grinding from the turbo, blue smoke, or a check engine light, usually at high mileage.
issues.why: The turbocharger on early RDXs wears out, and owners report failures around 90,000-125,000 miles. Acura used a different turbo design later.
issues.next: Have boost and turbo shaft play checked at the first sign of power loss or smoke. Change oil on time, since turbos rely on clean oil.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pressure sensor
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine or oil spots on the driveway, often near the oil filter area.
issues.why: RepairPal says the most reported RDX problem is an engine oil leak, tied to the oil pressure sensor on 2007-2012 models.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed. Replacing the sensor is a small job; keep an eye on the oil level until it is done.

issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with RPM, sometimes with low oil pressure.
issues.why: Owners report connecting rod bearing failures on 2007 RDXs, usually at high mileage.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it checked if a knock starts. Engine repair or replacement is usually needed.

issues.sym: Warning lights, the gear indicator flashing, or erratic shifting.
issues.why: Owners report a failing gear position sensor on the automatic transmission.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. Replacing the sensor usually fixes it.

issues.t: A/C condenser damaged by road debris
issues.sym: The A/C stops blowing cold, sometimes soon after a highway trip.
issues.why: Owners report stones and road debris puncturing the A/C condenser behind the front grille, letting refrigerant leak out.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested. A grille screen can help protect a new condenser.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or the compressor makes noise when it engages.
issues.why: Owners report the A/C compressor failing around 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the system checked. A failed compressor should be replaced along with a system flush.

issues.sym: Fog or water inside a headlight, dim light or a burned-out bulb.
issues.why: The headlight housings can let moisture in, which dims the beam and can damage the bulb and ballast.
issues.next: Have the housing seal checked. A new headlight assembly is usually needed if water keeps getting in.

issues.sym: Red fluid spots under the car or a low transmission fluid level.
issues.why: Owners of 2010 RDXs report transmission leaks at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Have the leak located and fixed, and keep the fluid at the right level with Acura ATF.

issues.t: Check engine, VSA and SH-AWD lights all on
issues.sym: The check engine, stability control (VSA) and SH-AWD warning lights come on together.
issues.why: On Acuras, an engine fault often turns off the stability and AWD systems too, so several lights come on at once.
issues.next: Have the engine codes read first; fixing the engine fault normally clears the other lights.

issues.sym: Clicking or clunking when turning, vibration, or noise while driving.
issues.why: Owners report cracked axles and excessive drivetrain noise on 2012 RDXs.
issues.next: Have the axles, boots and mounts inspected. Replace a cracked axle right away.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights fail or are very dim
issues.sym: Low beams very dim or not working, making night driving hard.
issues.why: Hundreds of owners filed complaints about the low beams on 2013-2015 RDXs, which often involve the headlight bulbs, ballasts or assemblies.
issues.next: Check the bulbs first. If they are fine, have the headlight ballast and assembly tested.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead or won't start
issues.sym: The engine cranks slowly or won't start, especially after sitting.
issues.why: Owners report repeated dead batteries; a weak battery or an electrical drain are the usual causes.
issues.next: Have the battery load-tested and the system checked for a parasitic drain.

issues.sym: A clang or knock from the rear when going over bumps or potholes.
issues.why: Owners report rear suspension noise on 2013 RDXs, usually from worn links, bushings or shock mounts.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected and any worn parts replaced.

issues.sym: Warning lights, a no-start or systems acting strangely, with chewed wires under the hood.
issues.why: Owners report rodents chewing the soy-based wire insulation, which can be expensive to repair.
issues.next: Have the wiring inspected. Rodent-deterrent tape on repaired wiring helps prevent repeat damage.

issues.sym: The engine stumbles, misfires or stalls, with a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners of 2015 RDXs report stalls and misfires; ignition coils, spark plugs or fuel delivery are common causes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the misfiring cylinder found.

issues.sym: Hesitation when accelerating, hard or sluggish shifts, or a shudder at low speed.
issues.why: Owners of 2016-2018 RDXs report transmission hesitation and shudder that often improves with a software update or fluid change.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about software updates and fluid service before major repairs.

issues.sym: Squealing, squeaking or grinding from the brakes, often in the first few thousand miles.
issues.why: Brake squeal is one of the most reported RDX complaints. Vibration between pads and rotors causes it.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected; new pads, shims and grease usually stop the noise.

issues.sym: A pulsing brake pedal or a shaking steering wheel when braking.
issues.why: Owners of 2017 RDXs report warped front rotors at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and resurfaced or replaced.

issues.sym: Navigation errors, or AcuraLink connected services not working.
issues.why: Owners report navigation and AcuraLink failures on 2017-2018 RDXs.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for software updates and confirm your AcuraLink subscription is active.

issues.t: Sudden power loss or limp mode
issues.sym: The engine suddenly loses power while accelerating or passing, the speed drops to about 15-40 mph, and a check engine light may come on. It often runs normally after a restart.
issues.why: Owners report limp mode on the 2.0L turbo. One documented fix was an intercooler replacement and an engine computer update. The fuel pump recall can also cause stalling.
issues.next: Check for the fuel pump recall first. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer to check the intercooler and engine software.

issues.sym: The screen freezes, Apple CarPlay drops out, Bluetooth audio skips, or FM/XM radio won't play.
issues.why: Owners report software glitches in the RDX infotainment system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for software updates. Restarting the car often clears a frozen screen.

issues.sym: The rear glass suddenly breaks with no object hitting it.
issues.why: Owners of 2021 RDXs report rear windows shattering on their own.
issues.next: Report it to NHTSA and ask Acura about goodwill coverage. Check your insurance glass coverage.

issues.sym: A vibration felt in the steering wheel and through the car.
issues.why: Owners report vibration on new 2023 RDXs; wheel balance and tires are the first things to check.
issues.next: Have the wheels balanced and tires checked for flat spots or defects.

issues.sym: The A/C suddenly stops cooling.
issues.why: Owners of 2025 RDXs report road pebbles puncturing the A/C condenser and letting refrigerant leak out.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested. Check whether new-car warranty or insurance covers it.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The Takata driver airbag inflator can burst when it deploys and throw metal fragments.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 16V061 and 19V182 today. The fix is free.

issues.t: Engine stalls from failing fuel pump (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, won't start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The fuel pump in the tank can fail. Acura recalled these RDXs under several campaigns.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 20V314, 21V215 and 23V858 and get the free pump replacement.

issues.t: Seat belt may not latch properly (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt that seems latched but releases, or a buckle warning.
issues.why: A seat belt buckle may not latch fully, so it may not hold the occupant in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V158.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may deploy incorrectly (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: Acura recalled these RDXs because an airbag may deploy incorrectly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V064.

issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power, or the SUV rolling when parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: A small number of 2021 RDXs were recalled for a driveshaft that can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V939 and always set the parking brake.

issues.t: Shifter can leave Park without the brake (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves out of Park without pressing the brake pedal.
issues.why: A brake-shift interlock fault could let the SUV roll away.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V143.

issues.sym: The brake pedal goes lower than normal, or the SUV may move unexpectedly.
issues.why: A small batch of 2023 RDXs was recalled for a brake problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V430.

issues.t: Steering gear can corrode and bind (recall)
issues.sym: Steering feels stiff or notchy, or binds.
issues.why: A small number of 2024 RDXs have steering gears that can corrode and bind.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V114 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering with warning messages
issues.sym: Steering assist cuts out or the wheel becomes very hard to turn, often while turning at 35-55 mph, with power steering, brake and driver-assist warnings on the dash. It often comes back after a restart.
issues.why: Many 2025 RDX owners have filed NHTSA complaints describing the electric power steering shutting off. Acura has not named a cause for the RDX in these reports.
issues.next: Pull over safely, then restart. Report every event to the dealer and NHTSA, and ask the dealer to save the fault codes and check for any recall on your VIN.

issues.sym: The SUV brakes on its own or the brakes feel reduced, along with collision mitigation, lane keeping or brake system warnings.
issues.why: Owners of 2025 RDXs report the safety systems braking unexpectedly or shutting off together, often at the same time as power steering warnings.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer and NHTSA, have the codes saved, and check for software updates or recalls.
